title: Sunday Quick Tip
subtitle: Talk at their height
hook: Next time you explain a drill, try kneeling down.
intro: You stand and explain to a circle of eight-year-olds.
Half of them are looking at your cleats.
statement: Kids listen better when you meet them where they are.
q1: Do you kneel down when you talk to young players —
q2: or stand so the whole group can see you?
q3: What changes in their faces when you kneel?
t1: There is no perfect answer here. But listening improves
t2: when kids can see your face.
cta: Coaches — do you kneel or stand?
ctaLines: Kneel for one player. Stand for the group.
Eye level or easy to see?
ctaPrompt: Share your communication habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
Next time you explain a drill, try kneeling down.
You stand and explain to a circle of eight-year-olds. Half of them are looking at your cleats.
Kids listen better when you meet them where they are.
Kneel at their level or stand where all can see. Both can work.
Do you kneel or stand? Share your habit in the comments.
